passage:
A city park stopped cutting one large grass area every week. Instead, it let wildflowers grow and cut only walking paths.
At first, some visitors complained that the park looked messy. Then butterflies, bees, and birds became more common. Signs explained that the area was managed for wildlife.
Children enjoyed walking through the paths and looking for insects.
The park did not abandon care. It changed what care looked like.
A neat lawn is easy to understand, but nature does not always grow in straight lines. The rewilded park taught visitors that beauty can be active, moving, and a little untidy.
